questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The impulse of a force is equal to the change in momentum it produces. Its SI unit is:
questions.explanation: Impulse = F × t, so its unit is newton second, which is the same as kg m s⁻¹, the unit of momentum.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 11, Chapter 4: Laws of Motion

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two projectiles are thrown with the same speed at angles of 30° and 60° to the horizontal. Their horizontal ranges are:
questions.explanation: R = u² sin 2θ / g, and sin 60° equals sin 120°, so complementary angles always give the same range even though the maximum heights and times of flight differ.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 11, Chapter 3: Motion in a Plane

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The frequency of revolution of a charged particle in a cyclotron is independent of:
options: The speed and the radius of the path
questions.explanation: The cyclotron frequency is qB/2πm. As the particle speeds up its radius grows in the same proportion, so the time per revolution stays fixed, which is why one steady radio frequency can keep accelerating it.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 12, Chapter 4: Moving Charges and Magnetism

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Avogadro's law states that under the same conditions of temperature and pressure, equal volumes of all gases contain:
questions.explanation: The law counts molecules, not atoms or mass, and it is what lets gas volume ratios in a reaction be read directly as mole ratios.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 11, Chapter 1: Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The number of spectral lines produced when an electron in a hydrogen atom returns from the 4th energy level to the ground state is:
questions.explanation: The number of lines is n(n - 1)/2 = 4 × 3/2 = 6, counting every possible downward transition between the four levels.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 11, Chapter 2: Structure of Atom

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The dipole moment of NH₃ is greater than that of NF₃ although fluorine is more electronegative than hydrogen. This is because in NH₃:
options: There is no lone pair on nitrogen
The lone pair moment and the bond moments point in the same direction, while in NF₃ they oppose each other
questions.explanation: In NH₃ the N-H bond moments point towards nitrogen, adding to the lone pair moment. In NF₃ the N-F moments point away from nitrogen and partly cancel it, so the net moment is small.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 11, Chapter 4: Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Methanogens, halophiles and thermoacidophiles are grouped together as:
options: Archaebacteria, which live in extreme habitats
questions.explanation: Their distinctive cell wall lets them survive salty, hot or acidic conditions. Methanogens live in the gut of ruminants and produce the methane of biogas.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Pteridophytes differ from bryophytes mainly in that pteridophytes:
options: Possess vascular tissue and a dominant sporophyte
Lack any need for water in fertilisation
questions.explanation: Pteridophytes are the first land plants with xylem and phloem, and the plant body we see is the sporophyte. They still need water for fertilisation and form no seeds.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Vital capacity of the lungs is defined as:
options: The maximum volume of air a person can breathe out after a forced inspiration
The air left after a forced expiration
The air breathed in during one normal breath
questions.explanation: Vital capacity equals ERV + TV + IRV and is about 4.5 litres in a healthy adult. It leaves out the residual volume, which can never be expelled.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 14: Breathing and Exchange of Gases

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Lymph differs from blood in that lymph:
options: Contains red blood cells but no plasma
Lacks red blood cells and most plasma proteins but is rich in lymphocytes
questions.explanation: Lymph returns tissue fluid and proteins to the blood, carries lymphocytes for immunity, and the lacteals of the intestinal villi use it to absorb digested fats.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 15: Body Fluids and Circulation
